name: Input
purpose: Accept user, document, web, email, API, and multimodal signals into the agent runtime before any model processing begins.
inputs: Web pages and third-party API payloads
Images, audio, and other multimodal content
processing: Sanitization and isolation of untrusted payloads
Human confirmation gates for high-consequence requests
dependencies: Policy for trusted vs untrusted sources
trustBoundaries: Untrusted external content enters a control plane that may treat text as instruction
Caller identity and source authenticity are asserted across systems
Multimodal payloads cross modality-specific parsers with uneven controls
threatActors: External attackers via prompts or poisoned documents
attackSurfaces: Multimodal payloads with steganographic or OCR-borne instructions
Untrusted external content and social engineering
failureModes: Over-trust of authenticated but compromised senders
propagationPaths: Injected instructions survive into tokenization and context assembly
Primed goals skew inference and planning
Tool selection and execution inherit attacker intent
Poisoned content can be written into memory for lasting compromise
consequences: Loss of audit integrity for downstream decisions

prevent: Instruction/data separation with explicit trust labels
Content isolation and sandboxing for untrusted documents
detect: Rate and novelty alerts on inbound content
recover: Revoke grants issued under tainted input
verify: Adversarial input test suites with pass/fail evidence
Blocked-action evidence for rejected high-risk requests

exampleScenario.initialCondition: A support agent ingests a customer PDF attachment into an operations assistant.
exampleScenario.failureOrAttack: The PDF embeds white-on-white instructions to export CRM records and email them externally.
exampleScenario.propagation: Hidden text is tokenized, assembled into context, and influences planning and tool selection.
exampleScenario.consequence: Customer PII is exfiltrated through an authorized connector.
exampleScenario.countermeasure: Treat attachments as untrusted data; isolate content; require human confirmation before export tools.
exampleScenario.validation: Red-team PDF suite blocked; signed deny receipt for export tool; quarantine log with provenance.

residualRisk: Trusted channels can still carry compromised content
Human confirmations can be fatigued or social-engineered
trustBoundary: Untrusted external content enters a control plane that may treat text as instruction
representativeVulnerabilities: Multimodal payloads with steganographic or OCR-borne instructions
controlOpportunities: Instruction/data separation with explicit trust labels
Adversarial input test suites with pass/fail evidence

name: Tokenization
purpose: Normalize and tokenize text (and related modalities) into the discrete units models and scanners consume.
processing: Alignment checks between raw text and token stream
outputs: Token stream for model and policy path
dependencies: Scanner pipelines that must stay aligned
trustBoundaries: Security controls that inspect raw text may disagree with the model token view
Normalization alters meaning before either path sees content
threatActors: Attackers crafting token-boundary and encoding tricks
Insiders tuning budgets to evade review
attackSurfaces: Mismatch between raw-text scanners and token streams
propagationPaths: Bypassed filters allow malicious instructions into context assembly
Truncated policy text weakens later constraint enforcement
Budget exhaustion degrades monitoring quality

contain: Hard fail on unsafe control characters
verify: Differential tests: scanner vs model path

exampleScenario.initialCondition: A policy scanner blocks the phrase "ignore previous instructions" in UTF-8.
exampleScenario.failureOrAttack: An attacker encodes the same intent with homoglyphs and zero-width characters that the model still interprets.
exampleScenario.propagation: The token stream carries the instruction into context assembly while the scanner reports clean.
exampleScenario.consequence: Downstream planning treats attacker text as system instruction.
exampleScenario.countermeasure: Canonicalize before both scanner and model; compare raw and token views; fail closed on residual invisibles.
exampleScenario.validation: Fixture suite shows scanner and model agree; blocked samples produce deny evidence.

residualRisk: Multimodal token paths with uneven coverage
trustBoundary: Security controls that inspect raw text may disagree with the model token view
controlOpportunities: Differential tests: scanner vs model path

name: Context Assembly
purpose: Assemble system prompts, user content, retrieved knowledge, tool results, and memory into the working context window.
trustBoundaries: Retrieved and tool-returned text must not inherit system trust
Cross-tenant and cross-user data must not co-mingle
Stale policy may silently weaken constraints
failureModes: Boundary collapse between system and untrusted text
propagationPaths: Poisoned context steers inference
Lost constraints enable unsafe planning and tool use
Leaked system prompts aid further attacks

recover: Rebuild context from pinned trusted sources

exampleScenario.initialCondition: A RAG assistant retrieves top-k docs for a billing dispute.
exampleScenario.failureOrAttack: An attacker plants a high-similarity doc that elevates itself and embeds override instructions.
exampleScenario.propagation: Poisoned retrieval dominates context; inference and planning follow attacker goals.
exampleScenario.consequence: Unauthorized account credit is issued via tools.
exampleScenario.countermeasure: Retrieval allowlists, provenance scoring, pinned policies, and constraint-preservation tests.
exampleScenario.validation: Poisoned-doc red team blocked; retrieval audit shows source deny; signed decision for tool deny.

trustBoundary: Retrieved and tool-returned text must not inherit system trust

name: Inference
purpose: Generate candidate tokens, conclusions, and action proposals under model uncertainty.
trustBoundaries: Model output is untrusted until validated
Provider routing changes trust and residual risk
Safety classifiers are themselves fallible controls
propagationPaths: False conclusions become plan premises
Unsafe completions propose dangerous tools
Leaked secrets enter later context or memory

contain: Force human review for consequential conclusions
recover: Re-run with pinned model and schema

exampleScenario.initialCondition: A clinical triage assistant proposes a next-step recommendation.
exampleScenario.failureOrAttack: The model hallucinates a contraindicated medication with high confidence.
exampleScenario.propagation: Planning encodes the drug into an order workflow; tools prepare a prescription action.
exampleScenario.countermeasure: Structured output, formulary allowlist checks, secondary verification, human review for clinical conclusions.
exampleScenario.validation: Deterministic formulary reject; secondary model disagreement alert; HITL approval record.

trustBoundary: Model output is untrusted until validated

name: Planning
purpose: Bind goals, decompose tasks, sequence steps, and estimate blast radius before tools are chosen.
trustBoundaries: Plans must not expand authority beyond granted scope
Intermediate steps can hide irreversible actions
Trust-before-execution patterns apply to high-consequence plan commits
threatActors: Operators approving oversized plans under pressure
attackSurfaces: Unsafe sequencing and hidden intermediate actions
propagationPaths: Unsafe plans force risky tool selection
Hidden steps reach execution without scrutiny
Budget blowouts degrade monitoring

exampleScenario.initialCondition: An infra agent is asked to "fix latency" on a production service.
exampleScenario.failureOrAttack: Injected context expands the goal to rebuild clusters and rotate all credentials.
exampleScenario.propagation: Tool selection pulls destructive cloud APIs; execution would mutate production.
exampleScenario.countermeasure: Goal binding, blast-radius analysis, protected-action detection, and human approval before irreversible plans.
exampleScenario.validation: Plan rejected with STEP_UP evidence; no tool calls issued; signed plan-deny receipt.

trustBoundary: Plans must not expand authority beyond granted scope
representativeVulnerabilities: Unsafe sequencing and hidden intermediate actions

name: Tool Selection
purpose: Choose concrete tools and connectors from a catalog based on the validated plan and granted capabilities.
trustBoundaries: Tool catalogs and descriptions are part of the attack surface
Confused-deputy risk when tools act with broader authority
Trust-before-execution applies before binding powerful tools
propagationPaths: Wrong tool reaches execution with real credentials
Hostile parameters become side effects
Shadow tools bypass monitoring

recover: Roll back to pinned tool versions

exampleScenario.initialCondition: A developer agent needs to open a pull request.
exampleScenario.failureOrAttack: A poisoned MCP tool description steers selection to a lookalike that exfiltrates tokens.
exampleScenario.propagation: Execution invokes the hostile connector with repo credentials.
exampleScenario.consequence: Source code and secrets leave the tenant.
exampleScenario.countermeasure: Signed registry, allowlists, identity verification, least privilege, pinned versions.
exampleScenario.validation: Unsigned tool rejected; selection audit shows allowlist miss; no credential use on deny.

residualRisk: Metadata that is signed but still malicious
trustBoundary: Tool catalogs and descriptions are part of the attack surface

name: Execution
purpose: Invoke tools and produce real-world side effects where language becomes consequence.
trustBoundaries: Authority must be proven before side effects
Fail-open behavior is a critical control defect
Trust-before-execution and signed evidence apply at this layer
threatActors: Attackers who reached this layer via earlier compromise
propagationPaths: Successful malicious execution poisons memory and future context
Stolen credentials enable further campaigns
Irreversible changes permanently alter production

verify: Signed execution receipts (identity, action, resource, decision, policy, trust/risk, time)

exampleScenario.initialCondition: A finance agent prepares a vendor payment under an approved plan.
exampleScenario.failureOrAttack: Parameter injection changes the destination account after approval.
exampleScenario.propagation: Without re-authorization, funds leave the organization; memory may record a false "paid" fact.
exampleScenario.consequence: Direct financial loss and audit failure.
exampleScenario.countermeasure: Bind approved parameters cryptographically; re-authorize mutations; fail closed; emit signed receipts.
exampleScenario.validation: Mutation triggers STEP_UP; deny receipt for changed IBAN; no payment posted.

trustBoundary: Authority must be proven before side effects
controlOpportunities: Signed execution receipts (identity, action, resource, decision, policy, trust/risk, time)

name: Memory
purpose: Persist short-term and long-term state that re-enters future context assembly — a feedback loop, not a terminal stage.
inputs: Summaries and facts proposed for durability
trustBoundaries: Durable writes require higher trust than ephemeral turns
Memory retrieval re-enters context assembly with lasting influence
Trust-before-execution applies to memory writes and high-impact retrieval
propagationPaths: Poisoned memory re-enters context assembly on later sessions
Stale or false facts steer inference and planning indefinitely
Sensitive residues create compliance exposure across runs
consequences: Loss of organizational trust in the agent

prevent: Human review for durable high-impact facts

exampleScenario.initialCondition: An assistant stores "prefer vendor X" after a poisoned support thread.
exampleScenario.failureOrAttack: The false preference is written without provenance or approval.
exampleScenario.propagation: Future context assembly retrieves the preference; planning and tools favor vendor X repeatedly.
exampleScenario.consequence: Ongoing procurement bias and potential fraud.
exampleScenario.countermeasure: Authorize durable writes, attach provenance, quarantine low-trust facts, verify deletion on revoke.
exampleScenario.validation: Unauthorized write denied; quarantine record; post-delete retrieval returns empty with evidence.

trustBoundary: Durable writes require higher trust than ephemeral turns
